overview: This five-page Department of State file register indexes papers from 1930–1938 concerning disabled, wrecked, stranded, and salvaged Japanese merchant vessels. The cases include American assistance to the Daiichi Ume Maru, Shito Maru, Suwa Maru, Choshun Maru, and No. 8 Sumiyoshi Maru; the Midori Maru–Senzan Maru and Taiyo–Dependable collisions; and the prolonged dispute over salvage of the Kowa Maru in Philippine waters. Later entries focus on whether Japanese salvage vessels should receive access to Philippine and American territorial waters on a reciprocal basis, with comparisons to Japanese practice and the President Hoover incident. The register also supplies cross-references to correspondence filed elsewhere in the State Department decimal system.

subfiles.title: List of Papers: Disabled, Wrecked and Stranded Japanese Merchant Vessels, Items 49–72
subfiles.about: A register of correspondence concerning Japanese shipwrecks, collisions, rescues, and the legal conditions governing Japanese salvage operations in Philippine and other territorial waters.
subfiles.summary: The register summarizes papers dated chiefly from 1930 through 1938, beginning with Japanese expressions of thanks for American assistance to distressed ships and fishermen. Its largest group of entries concerns the stranded Kowa Maru and interdepartmental consideration of whether Japanese salvors could operate in Philippine waters under treaty law, local restrictions, or a principle of reciprocity. Other entries cover the sinking of the Midori Maru, the refusal of a Japanese tug to assist the President Hoover in restricted naval waters, and the Taiyo–Dependable collision near Guaymas. The final entry directs that reciprocal treatment of shipwrecked Japanese nationals and vessels be addressed through diplomatic channels at Taihoku.

interest: Tracks 1930s Japanese maritime rescues, gratitude, and jurisdictional disputes, cross-referenced across several decimal files.
